newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 31.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Spy bureau to tap overseas calls: The Government Communications Security Bureau, New Zealand's hi-tech eavesdropper, has been given extra powers allowing it to listen on international telephone calls by foreign people or organisations. Page 1.

Peters' super plan a nightmare says Upton: Environment Minister Simon Upton described Treasurer Winston Peters' retirement savings scheme as a regulatory nightmare -- on the eve of publication of a superannuation review tipped to say
there is no need to switch from the present pay-as-you-go system. Page 1.

Consumers Institute rejects super: The Consumers Institute has come out against the government's proposed compulsory retirement savings scheme, saying some people could be left thousands of dollars worse off. Page 2.
Easter trading bill thrown out: Parliament killed a bill on Wednesday night which would have allowed shops to open on Easter Sunday. Page 2.
Fernz says record profit unlikely to be repeated: Chemicals company Fernz Corporation lifted tax-paid profit by 7.5 percent to a record $46.8 million for the year ended May 31. Page 15.

Committee to hear evidence on Kopu: The privileges committee has decided to hear the evidence about whether newly independent MP Alamein Kopu should remain in Parliament, rather than refer the case to the Court of Appeal. Page 2.

IRD warns employers about compliance costs: Employers would have to pay between 50 cents and $1 a transaction for each employee to comply with the proposed retirement savings scheme, Parliament's finance and expenditure committee was told on Wednesday. Page 2.
Business 'sees light at end of tunnel': After heading down for almost a year, business confidence bounced back in July, breaking a "dismal trend", according to the National Bank. Page 15.

S & P lifts Brierley's credit rating one notch: Brierley Investments' corporate credit rating has been lifted a notch to BBB from BBB-minus, with a stable outlook, by international credit rating agency Standard and Poor's. Page 15.

Present super scheme may be better -- expert: The existing pay-as-you-go state pension scheme may be better than the proposed compulsory retirement savings scheme, according to National Bank chief economist Brendan O'Donavan. Page 15.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Property assets float planned by AMP: The country's largest fund manager, AMP Society, plans a property float of assets thought to be worth $500 million.
THE PRESS

Chch rates to rise 3.12pc: Christchurch City ratepayers face an average general rates rise of 3.12 percent after the city council budgeted on Wednesday night to include a controversial $1.1 million programme of social cohesion. Page 1.
Support for no-advert TV station: Pressure is mounting on the government to hold an investigation into the cost of running a non-commercial television station. Page 4.
SE Utilities doubles dividend: South Eastern Utilities has more than doubled its divident rate in its latest year. Page 30.
Macraes Mining axes 66 jobs: Macraes Mining is slashing 66 jobs from its workforce to save $19 million in annual costs. Page 30.
Terminal cancer forces Makin to quit: Andrew Makin has resigned all his directorships after learning he has terminal cancer, the "Business Herald" reports. Page 30.
TimberWest sale gives boost to FCC result: The sale of TimberWest boosted Fletcher Challenge Canada's final quarter and annual results. Page 31.
